quotes.text: I look forward to reviewing specific bills regarding AI regulations and AI workforce development as they make their way through Congress.

I think it would be very difficult for companies to navigate when you have 50 different specs of regulation that … they have to comply with, just because their product is very easily used in multiple states.
I think the worst possible thing we could do is try to have government bureaucrats figuring out or setting the rules for what AI can and cannot be. We've got to let the market develop that.

America should lead the world in artificial intelligence, but we must ensure hardworking families and small businesses are not asked to subsidize the enormous energy demands of data centers. The principle is simple: data centers should be located in communities that choose to host them, those communities should share in the economic benefits they bring, and the data centers should pay their own way. The Ratepayer Protection Act will help ensure the companies driving the need for costly new energy infrastructure bear those costs, not existing ratepayers.
